X is one of the two, drawn afresh for every trial: hear A, B and X as often as you like on the song playing, then say which X was. A change is heard a few moments after you press, within the audio already buffered.

A is the equaliser as set, B is the signal with it bypassed. Each is lowered, never raised, until their loudness across 20 Hz to 16 kHz agrees to 0.1 dB, so the louder one cannot give itself away. %1$s The room correction stays on in both. Editing the curve ends the comparison.

A is lossy restoration as set, B the setting you choose. Restoration changes how loud a song plays, so the song is first measured through both, which takes a moment, and the louder is lowered, never raised, until the two agree. A lossless file is touched by neither. %1$s

A is the resampler as set, B the quality and phase you choose. Both play at one level. The resampler works only where the song\'s rate has to be changed to the device\'s; where it does not, the two sound alike and the test is refused. %1$s

A is the dither as the phone plays it, B the kind you choose. Both play at one level. Dither works only where the bits are cut down to the device\'s depth; where they are not, the two sound alike and the test is refused. %1$s
